q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 27,00,000 and the Net Tonne Kilometres performed are 90,00,000. The average rate realised per tonne kilometre is:
e: Average rate per tonne kilometre = goods earnings / Net Tonne Kilometres = Rs 27,00,000 / 90,00,000 = Rs 0.30.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the carriage of a dog by a passenger train, a dog box is provided in the brake van or luggage van, and the dog is carried therein on payment of the prescribed charges.
2. Dogs are permitted to be carried free of charge in any passenger compartment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a dog is carried in the dog box in the brake or luggage van on payment of the prescribed charges. Statement 2 is wrong: dogs are not carried free in passenger compartments.

q: Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed are levied:

options.A: At a flat rate for all periods of detention
options.B: Only for the first day of detention
options.C: At rates which increase (escalate) as the period of detention lengthens
options.D: At rates which decrease as the period of detention lengthens

e: Demurrage is levied on an escalating scale: the longer the wagon is detained beyond the free time, the higher the rate, so as to discourage detention.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are 5,60,00,000 and the loaded wagon kilometres are 16,00,000. The average load of a loaded wagon is:

options.C: 40 tonnes
options.D: 35 tonnes

e: Average load of a loaded wagon = Net Tonne Kilometres / loaded wagon kilometres = 5,60,00,000 / 16,00,000 = 35 tonnes.

q: In parcel traffic, the parcel charges are:

options.A: Required to be prepaid at the time of booking
options.B: Always collected at the destination station as 'to-pay' charges
options.C: Billed to the consignee month by month
options.D: Recovered only after weighment of the parcels at the destination

e: Parcel traffic is booked on a prepaid basis: the parcel charges must be paid at the booking station at the time of booking.

q: In order to prevent misdespatch and loss of consignments, the goods tariff requires that every package of a consignment booked by rail must bear:

options.A: The telephone number of the consignor
options.B: The value of the contents of the package
options.C: Distinct identification marks and the name of the destination station
options.D: The seal of the forwarding station

e: Every package must bear distinct identification marks and the name of the destination station, so that it can be correctly sorted, despatched and delivered without misdespatch.

q: Under the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS), the module which deals with the allotment of rakes against the demands registered by freight customers is the:

options.C: Crew Management System
options.D: Rake Allotment System

e: Under FOIS, the Rake Allotment System is the module that allots rakes against the demands registered by freight customers; rake monitoring and terminal functions are handled by other modules.

q: Registered newspapers and periodicals offered for carriage by passenger trains are charged:

options.C: At goods trainload rates
options.D: At full luggage rates

e: Registered newspapers and periodicals sent by passenger trains are charged at special concessional parcel rates, not at the ordinary or highest parcel scales.

q: Advance booking of unreserved tickets for long-distance journeys is permitted at stations and through the Unreserved Ticketing System:

options.A: Up to 7 days in advance for all journeys
options.B: Only on the day of the journey
options.C: Up to 30 days in advance for all journeys
options.D: Up to 3 days in advance, where the distance of the journey exceeds 200 kilometres

e: Advance booking of unreserved tickets through UTS is allowed up to 3 days in advance only where the journey exceeds 200 kilometres; shorter journeys are booked on the day of travel.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On a train, the Travelling Ticket Examiner may allot accommodation of a higher class to a passenger, subject to availability, on payment of the difference of fare.
2. Such on-board upgradation by the Travelling Ticket Examiner is made free of charge in all cases.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the TTE may upgrade a passenger to a higher class, subject to availability, on collecting the difference of fare. Statement 2 is wrong: the upgradation is not free.

q: A freight customer can trace the position and movement of his consignment booked through the Freight Operations Information System by quoting:

options.A: The number of the wagon in which it was loaded only
options.C: The code of the siding at which it was booked
options.D: The Railway Receipt (RR) number of the consignment

e: FOIS consignment tracking is done through the Railway Receipt number, which uniquely identifies the consignment from booking to delivery.

q: An 'ambush check' in connection with ticket checking on the Railways means:

options.A: A check of tickets conducted only at the destination station
options.B: A check conducted jointly with the Railway Magistrate
options.C: A surprise check in which the ticket checking squad boards the train at an unscheduled intermediate point in order to detect ticketless travel
options.D: A check of the accounts rendered by the ticket checking staff

e: An ambush check is a surprise ticket check in which the squad boards the train at an unscheduled intermediate point, catching ticketless travellers who expect checks only at known points.

q: Milk traffic from the producing centres to the metropolitan cities is carried by the Railways in:

options.C: Insulated parcel vans only
options.D: Passenger coaches attached to mail trains

e: Milk is carried in special milk tank wagons, which are designed to move bulk milk hygienically and quickly from producing centres to the metropolitan cities.

q: Where a consignment carried in a sealed wagon arrives at the destination station with its seals intact, the position regarding re-weighment of the consignment at the destination is that re-weighment:

options.A: Must be granted free of charge as a matter of right
options.B: Cannot be claimed by the consignee as a matter of right
options.C: Can be ordered only by the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: Is carried out in all cases at the cost of the Railways

e: Where a sealed wagon arrives with seals intact, there is no prima facie evidence of loss or tampering, so the consignee cannot claim re-weighment as a matter of right.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 96,00,000 and the engine days during the period are 3,000. The Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day = 96,00,000 / 3,000 engine days = 3,200.

q: In the Passenger Reservation System, the abbreviation GNWL stands for:

options.C: Group Nomination Wait List
options.D: General Wagon List

e: GNWL stands for General Wait List, the waitlist for general-quota bookings in the Passenger Reservation System.

q: During a month, the goods locomotives of a railway consumed 6,300 litres of diesel oil and performed 18,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month is:

options.C: 3.5 litres per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.D: 4.5 litres per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres

e: SFC = fuel consumed / Gross Tonne Kilometres x 1000 = 6,300 / 18,00,000 x 1000 = 3.5 litres per 1000 GTKM.

q: Vande Bharat Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Indigenously designed semi-high speed self-propelled train sets which do not require a separate locomotive
options.B: Trains hauled by imported high-horsepower electric locomotives
options.C: Double-decker trains run exclusively on suburban sections
options.D: Freight trains run for the carriage of automobiles

e: Vande Bharat trains are indigenously designed semi-high speed, self-propelled train sets with distributed traction, so they need no separate locomotive.

q: In a month, the total wagon days on a railway were 5,60,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 1,60,000. The wagon turn-round for the month is:

options.C: 4.0 days
options.D: 3.5 days

e: Wagon turn-round = total wagon days / number of wagons loaded = 5,60,000 / 1,60,000 = 3.5 days.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The punctuality performance of passenger trains is assessed primarily with reference to their right-time arrival at the destination station.
2. Punctuality is assessed solely with reference to the right-time departure of trains from their originating stations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: punctuality of passenger trains is judged mainly by right-time arrival at the destination. Statement 2 is wrong: it is not assessed solely by departure from the originating station.

q: During a month, the locomotives in electric traction on a railway consumed 57,500 kWh of electrical energy and performed 25,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of the railway for the month is:

options.C: 25 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres
options.D: 30 kWh per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres

e: SEC = energy consumed / Gross Tonne Kilometres x 1000 = 57,500 / 25,00,000 x 1000 = 23 kWh per 1000 GTKM.

q: When the maximum prescribed waitlist limit for a train and class is reached, further requests for reservation in that train and class are declined with the status shown as:

options.C: REGRET
options.D: TQWL

e: When the prescribed maximum waitlist limit is reached, no further booking is accepted and the status is shown as REGRET.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 33,00,000 and the goods engine days during the period are 750. The Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day = 33,00,000 / 750 = 4,400.

q: Under the Railways Act, 1989, after the termination of transit, the responsibility of the railway administration in respect of the goods entrusted to it is that of:

options.B: A bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.C: A common carrier with absolute liability
options.D: A warehouseman without any liability

e: During transit the Railways have carrier liability, but after termination of transit their responsibility for the goods is only that of a bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 96,00,000 and the tonnes carried are 2,40,000. The average lead of goods traffic is:

options.C: 45 kilometres
options.D: 50 kilometres

e: Average lead of goods traffic = Net Tonne Kilometres / tonnes carried = 96,00,000 / 2,40,000 = 40 kilometres.

q: The Dedicated Freight Corridors of the Railways have been built and are operated by:

options.A: The zonal railways through which they pass
options.C: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited
options.D: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited

e: The Dedicated Freight Corridors are built and operated by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, a special purpose vehicle for the corridor project.

q: A railway performed 63,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the number of passengers carried was 1,40,000. The average lead of passenger traffic is:

options.C: 45 kilometres
options.D: 55 kilometres

e: Average lead of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / passengers carried = 63,00,000 / 1,40,000 = 45 kilometres.

q: Along with a season ticket, a passenger is issued:

options.A: A photo identity card, which he is required to carry with the season ticket during the journey
options.B: A reservation voucher for reserved coaches
options.C: A complimentary pass for one companion
options.D: A luggage allowance card for booking excess luggage

e: A photo identity card is issued with the season ticket and must be carried along with it, so that only the authorised holder uses the ticket.

q: The total cost of the goods services of a railway for a period is Rs 39,00,000 and the Net Tonne Kilometres performed are 15,00,000. The cost per Net Tonne Kilometre is:
e: Cost per Net Tonne Kilometre = total cost of goods services / Net Tonne Kilometres = Rs 39,00,000 / 15,00,000 = Rs 2.60.

q: Amrit Bharat Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Premium fully air-conditioned trains with dynamic fares
options.B: Suburban EMU services run in metropolitan cities
options.C: Long-distance trains with non-air-conditioned coaches, worked on the push-pull principle with locomotives at both ends, for affordable long-distance travel
options.D: Tourist trains run exclusively for foreign tourists

e: Amrit Bharat Express trains are non-air-conditioned long-distance trains worked on the push-pull principle with locomotives at both ends, providing affordable travel with improved coaches.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are 27,00,000 and the wagon days during the period are 75,000. The Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day are:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day = 27,00,000 / 75,000 wagon days = 36.

q: Where a consignment is diverted to a new destination at the request of the consignor, the freight on the consignment is charged:

options.A: For the distance by the route actually followed by the consignment to the new destination
options.B: Only up to the original destination, the onward carriage being free
options.C: At double the normal rate for the diverted portion
options.D: On the basis of the shortest route between the booking station and the new destination, regardless of the route followed

e: On diversion, freight is charged for the distance actually traversed by the route followed to the new destination, since the consignment is carried over that route.

q: A railway performed 51,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the seat kilometres offered were 68,00,000. The load factor (occupation ratio) of the coaching services is:

options.C: 80 per cent
options.D: 85 per cent

e: Load factor = passenger kilometres / seat kilometres offered x 100 = 51,00,000 / 68,00,000 x 100 = 75 per cent.

q: Tejas Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Non-air-conditioned trains run for the carriage of parcels
options.C: Premium fully air-conditioned trains whose fares are higher than those of comparable Shatabdi Express trains
options.D: Trains run exclusively for the carriage of automobiles

e: Tejas Express trains are premium fully air-conditioned services, and their fares are kept higher than those of comparable Shatabdi Express trains.

q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 1,05,00,000 and the wagon days during the period are 3,00,000. The earnings per wagon day are:

options.C: Rs 32
options.D: Rs 35

e: Earnings per wagon day = goods earnings / wagon days = Rs 1,05,00,000 / 3,00,000 = Rs 35.

q: Wharfage charges at a station are levied with reference to:

options.A: The weight of the goods and the period for which they remain on the station premises beyond the free time allowed for their removal
options.B: The number of wagons in which the goods were carried
options.C: A percentage of the freight paid on the consignment
options.D: The value of the goods as declared by the consignee

e: Wharfage is charged on the weight of the goods and the time they occupy station premises beyond the free time allowed for removal after unloading.

q: The gross earnings of a railway for a year are Rs 4,000 crore and its working expenses are Rs 3,760 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway is:

options.C: 92 per cent
options.D: 96 per cent

e: Operating Ratio = working expenses / gross earnings x 100 = Rs 3,760 crore / Rs 4,000 crore x 100 = 94 per cent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The consignor is responsible for the correctness of the particulars, such as the description and weight of the goods, furnished by him in the Forwarding Note.
2. Where the Railways suffer loss on account of incorrect particulars furnished by the consignor, the loss is recoverable from the consignor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the consignor is responsible for the particulars declared in the Forwarding Note, and any loss caused to the Railways by incorrect particulars is recoverable from him.

q: During a month, the locomotives of a railway ran 8,75,000 engine kilometres and the engine days numbered 2,500. The engine kilometres per engine day are:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day = 8,75,000 / 2,500 engine days = 350.

q: 'Clone trains' are run by the Railways primarily to:

options.A: Clear the heavy rush of waitlisted passengers on busy routes, broadly following the timetable and stoppages of the original train
options.B: Replace the original train when it is withdrawn for maintenance
options.C: Carry the overflow of goods traffic from congested goods sheds
options.D: Provide additional trains for the exclusive use of railway staff

e: Clone trains are run on busy routes to clear heavy waitlists, broadly following the timetable and stoppages of the original train.

q: A railway performed 98,00,000 passenger kilometres during a year in which the route kilometres open for traffic were 3,500. The density of passenger traffic on the railway is:

options.C: 3,000 passenger kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: 3,200 passenger kilometres per route kilometre

e: Density of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / route kilometres = 98,00,000 / 3,500 = 2,800 passenger kilometres per route kilometre.

q: The fare charged for travel by Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains:

options.A: Does not cover meals, which are always charged for separately
options.B: Covers meals only in Air-conditioned First Class
options.C: Is inclusive of the cost of meals served to the passengers during the journey
options.D: Is inclusive of the cost of retiring rooms at the destination station

e: The fares of Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains are composite fares, inclusive of the cost of meals served on board during the journey.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a year were 1,75,00,000 and the route kilometres open for traffic were 5,000. The density of goods traffic on the railway is:

options.A: 3,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre
options.B: 3,200 Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre
options.C: 3,400 Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: 3,500 Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre

e: Density of goods traffic = Gross Tonne Kilometres / route kilometres = 1,75,00,000 / 5,000 = 3,500 GTKM per route kilometre.

q: 'Consequential train accidents' on the Railways are those train accidents which:

options.A: Have serious repercussions in the form of loss of human life or injury to persons, damage to railway property or interruption of through traffic
options.C: Occur only at manned level crossing gates
options.D: Result in no damage to railway property at all

e: Consequential train accidents are those having serious repercussions, such as loss of life or injury, heavy damage to railway property or interruption of through traffic.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 1,26,00,000 and the engine days during the period are 3,600. The Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day = 1,26,00,000 / 3,600 = 3,500.

q: Rail Travellers' Service Agents (RTSAs) on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Agents authorised to sell unreserved tickets at halt stations
options.B: Contractors engaged for the loading and unloading of goods at stations
options.C: Agents licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets on behalf of passengers, charging them a prescribed service charge
options.D: Staff deputed by travel agencies to work at reservation counters

e: Rail Travellers' Service Agents are persons licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets on behalf of passengers, charging them a prescribed service charge.

q: During a period, the total wagon kilometres run on a railway were 80,00,000, of which the empty wagon kilometres were 28,00,000. The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres is:

options.C: 32 per cent
options.D: 35 per cent

e: Percentage of empty wagon kilometres = 28,00,000 / 80,00,000 x 100 = 35 per cent.

q: Under the flexi fare system applicable to certain premium trains, the base fare:

options.A: Increases in stages as the proportion of accommodation sold in the train goes up, subject to a prescribed ceiling
options.B: Remains fixed throughout the booking period
options.C: Decreases progressively as the date of journey approaches
options.D: Is determined by auction among the passengers

e: Under flexi fare, the base fare rises in stages as more accommodation is sold, up to a prescribed ceiling, so early bookers pay less than late bookers.

q: The total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 21,00,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 60,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre is:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre = cost of coaching services / passenger kilometres = Rs 21,00,000 / 60,00,000 = Rs 0.35.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A season ticket is valid for travel in the unreserved accommodation of the class for which it is issued.
2. A season ticket by itself entitles the holder to travel in reserved coaches without obtaining a reservation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: 1 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: a season ticket is valid only in the unreserved accommodation of its class. Statement 2 is wrong: it does not by itself permit travel in reserved coaches.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are 3,90,00,000 and the loaded wagon kilometres are 12,00,000. The average load of a loaded wagon is:

options.C: 34.0 tonnes
options.D: 32.5 tonnes

e: Average load of a loaded wagon = Net Tonne Kilometres / loaded wagon kilometres = 3,90,00,000 / 12,00,000 = 32.5 tonnes.

q: The Passenger Reservation System of Indian Railways is a countrywide networked system, which means that:

options.A: A passenger can reserve accommodation in any train from any computerised reservation centre, irrespective of the station from which the train starts
options.B: Reservation can be made only at the station from which the train originates
options.C: Reservation centres of one zonal railway cannot book trains of another zonal railway
options.D: Reservation is possible only through the internet and not at counters

e: The Passenger Reservation System is fully networked countrywide, so accommodation in any train can be reserved from any computerised reservation centre, wherever the train starts.

q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 42,00,000 and the Net Tonne Kilometres performed are 1,20,00,000. The average rate realised per tonne kilometre is:
e: Average rate per tonne kilometre = goods earnings / Net Tonne Kilometres = Rs 42,00,000 / 1,20,00,000 = Rs 0.35.

q: At the time of preparation of the reservation chart of a train, the passengers holding Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) tickets are:

options.A: Treated as waitlisted passengers for all purposes
options.C: Provided confirmed accommodation against the berths falling vacant through cancellations, in the order of their RAC priority
options.D: Required to purchase fresh tickets at the current booking counter

e: At chart preparation, RAC passengers are allotted the berths that fall vacant through cancellations, strictly in the order of their RAC priority.

q: A railway performed 68,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the passenger train kilometres run were 16,000. The average number of passengers carried per train is:
e: Average passengers per train = passenger kilometres / passenger train kilometres = 68,00,000 / 16,000 = 425.

q: For travel on an e-ticket booked through the internet, the correct position is that:

options.A: Any one of the passengers on the ticket must carry, during the journey, the prescribed proof of identity whose particulars were furnished at the time of booking
options.B: No proof of identity is required to be carried by any passenger on an e-ticket
options.C: Every passenger on the ticket must carry the same identity card
options.D: The identity proof is required only for passengers travelling in Air-conditioned classes

e: On an e-ticket, any one of the passengers must carry the prescribed identity proof whose particulars were given at booking; the others need not carry the same proof.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 2,40,00,000 and the goods train kilometres run are 60,000. The average net load of a goods train is:

options.C: 420 tonnes
options.D: 450 tonnes

e: Average net load of a goods train = Net Tonne Kilometres / goods train kilometres = 2,40,00,000 / 60,000 = 400 tonnes.

q: Duronto Express trains were originally introduced by the Railways as:

options.B: Trains carrying only parcels and luggage
options.C: Point-to-point services running between the originating and destination stations without any commercial halt en route, stopping only for technical purposes
options.D: Trains reserved exclusively for the holders of season tickets

e: Duronto Express trains were introduced as point-to-point services with no commercial halt en route; they stopped only at technical halts such as crew change points.

q: The total vehicle kilometres run by the coaching vehicles of a railway during a period are 1,80,00,000 and the vehicle days during the period are 60,000. The vehicle kilometres per vehicle day are:
e: Vehicle kilometres per vehicle day = 1,80,00,000 / 60,000 vehicle days = 300.

q: At every station of the Railways, a complaint book is maintained primarily to enable:

options.A: The station staff to record complaints against passengers
options.B: The Accounts department to record the results of internal check
options.C: Passengers to record their complaints and suggestions for the attention of the railway administration
options.D: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts to record his inspection remarks

e: The complaint book kept at every station is for passengers to record complaints and suggestions, which are then inquired into by the railway administration.

q: 'Vistadome' coaches provided on certain trains of Indian Railways are distinguished by:

options.A: Air-conditioned executive-class seating with on-board catering facilities
options.B: Large glass windows and a glass roof, enabling the passengers to view the scenery along the route
options.C: A double-decker seating arrangement for short-distance services
options.D: Sleeper berths fitted with individual entertainment screens

e: Vistadome coaches have large glass windows and a glass roof, giving passengers a panoramic view of the scenery on scenic routes.

q: During a month, the goods locomotives of a railway consumed 4,800 litres of diesel oil and performed 16,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month is:

options.C: 3.0 litres per 1000 GTKM
options.D: 4.8 litres per 1000 GTKM

e: SFC = fuel consumed / Gross Tonne Kilometres x 1000 = 4,800 / 16,00,000 x 1000 = 3.0 litres per 1000 GTKM.

q: 'Jan Shatabdi' Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Day trains with air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned chair car accommodation, with fares lower than those of Shatabdi Express trains
options.B: Fully air-conditioned overnight trains with sleeper berths
options.C: Unreserved trains run exclusively for suburban passengers
options.D: Luxury tourist trains run on heritage circuits

e: Jan Shatabdi Express trains are day trains with air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned chair cars, run at fares lower than those of Shatabdi Express trains.

q: Under Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989, where a person who has applied for compensation for a train accident desires immediate relief pending the determination of his claim, the interim relief is paid by:

options.A: The Railway Claims Tribunal, out of its own funds
options.B: The State Government of the place where the accident occurred
options.C: The insurance company with which the passenger is insured
options.D: The railway administration, pending determination of the compensation by the Claims Tribunal

e: Under Section 126, interim relief is paid by the railway administration itself to give the claimant immediate help, pending final determination of compensation by the Claims Tribunal.

q: In a month, the total wagon days on a railway were 6,30,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 1,40,000. The wagon turn-round for the month is:

options.C: 5.0 days
options.D: 4.0 days

e: Wagon turn-round = total wagon days / number of wagons loaded = 6,30,000 / 1,40,000 = 4.5 days.

q: 'Deen Dayalu' coaches provided on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Upgraded unreserved (general second class) coaches with amenities such as cushioned luggage racks, bio-toilets and mobile charging points
options.B: Air-conditioned coaches attached to trains for the use of railway officers
options.C: Coaches specially designed for the carriage of physically challenged passengers only
options.D: Parcel coaches attached to long-distance Mail/Express trains

e: Deen Dayalu coaches are upgraded unreserved second class coaches fitted with amenities like cushioned luggage racks, bio-toilets and mobile charging points.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A remission is the waiver, by the competent authority, of a charge such as demurrage or wharfage which has accrued but has not been paid.
2. A refund is the repayment of an amount which has already been collected from a party but is found not due or in excess of what was due.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: remission waives a charge that has accrued but is unpaid, while a refund repays money already collected but found not due or collected in excess.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 51,00,000 and the goods engine days during the period are 850. The Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day = 51,00,000 / 850 = 6,000.

q: 'Anubhuti' coaches on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Economy-class coaches attached to long-distance trains
options.B: Premium air-conditioned chair car coaches, with upgraded amenities, attached to certain Shatabdi Express trains
options.C: Inspection coaches reserved for senior railway officers
options.D: Coaches converted for the carriage of two-wheelers and cars

e: Anubhuti coaches are premium air-conditioned chair car coaches with upgraded amenities, attached to certain Shatabdi Express trains.

q: Monthly Season Tickets (MST) on Indian Railways are ordinarily issued for journeys not exceeding:

options.C: 200 kilometres
options.D: 250 kilometres

e: Monthly Season Tickets are ordinarily issued for short suburban-type journeys not exceeding 150 kilometres.

q: During a month, the locomotives in electric traction on a railway consumed 66,000 kWh of electrical energy and performed 30,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of the railway for the month is:

options.C: 22 kWh per 1000 GTKM
options.D: 25 kWh per 1000 GTKM

e: SEC = energy consumed / Gross Tonne Kilometres x 1000 = 66,000 / 30,00,000 x 1000 = 22 kWh per 1000 GTKM.

q: 'UDAY' Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fully unreserved trains run on short-distance routes
options.B: Trains composed of model-rake coaches with sleeper accommodation
options.C: Goods trains run for the movement of perishable traffic
options.D: Double-decker air-conditioned chair car trains run as overnight intercity services

e: UDAY Express trains are double-decker air-conditioned chair car services run as overnight intercity trains on busy routes.

q: In railway accounts and statistics, the traffic which a railway receives from, or hands over to, another railway at interchange points is termed:

options.C: Suburban traffic
options.D: Departmental traffic

e: Traffic received from or handed over to another railway at interchange points is called foreign traffic, as distinct from local traffic originating and terminating on the same railway.

q: A railway performed 78,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the number of passengers carried was 1,30,000. The average lead of passenger traffic is:

options.C: 65 kilometres
options.D: 50 kilometres

e: Average lead of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / passengers carried = 78,00,000 / 1,30,000 = 60 kilometres.

q: The 'Joint Parcel Product' (JPP) service for door-to-door delivery of parcels is a joint initiative of Indian Railways and:

options.B: The National Highways Authority of India
options.C: The Department of Posts (India Post)
options.D: The Container Corporation of India

e: The Joint Parcel Product is a door-to-door parcel delivery service run jointly by Indian Railways and the Department of Posts (India Post).

q: Demurrage is distinguished from wharfage in that demurrage is a charge levied for:

options.A: The detention of goods on railway premises after their unloading from wagons
options.B: The storage of luggage in the cloak room of a station
options.C: The occupation of railway land by a licensee beyond the licence period
options.D: The detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for their loading or unloading

e: Demurrage is charged for detaining the wagon itself beyond the free time for loading or unloading; wharfage, in contrast, relates to goods occupying station premises.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a period are 88,00,000 and the engine days during the period are 2,200. The Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day are:
e: Gross Tonne Kilometres per engine day = 88,00,000 / 2,200 = 4,000.

q: 'Mahamana' Express trains of Indian Railways are so named because they are provided with:

options.A: 'Model Rake' coaches fitted with modern passenger amenities
options.B: Locomotives manufactured at Banaras Locomotive Works
options.C: Additional coaches reserved for students and teachers
options.D: On-board libraries for the use of passengers

e: Mahamana Express trains use Model Rake coaches fitted with modern passenger amenities such as modular panels, improved toilets and LED lighting.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Interim relief under Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989 is paid by the Railway Claims Tribunal after it finally determines the compensation payable.
2. Any sum paid as interim relief is taken into account by the Railway Claims Tribunal while determining the amount of compensation finally payable.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong: interim relief is paid by the railway administration, not by the Tribunal after final determination. Statement 2 is correct: the interim relief paid is adjusted against the final compensation.

q: The total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 26,00,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 65,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre is:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre = cost of coaching services / passenger kilometres = Rs 26,00,000 / 65,00,000 = Rs 0.40.

q: In the case of the AC Three Tier Economy (3E) class introduced on Indian Railways, the fare charged, as compared with the fare for AC Three Tier class, is:

options.A: Higher, because of the additional berths provided in the coaches
options.B: The same as for AC Three Tier class
options.C: Higher during the peak season only
options.D: Lower than that for AC Three Tier class

e: AC Three Tier Economy class offers additional berths at a fare lower than that of the regular AC Three Tier class.

q: In goods traffic, a 'block rake' means:

options.A: A full train-load consignment booked by one party from one station to a single destination station
options.B: A rake which is blocked for departmental use during emergencies
options.C: A rake formed of wagons belonging to different owning railways
options.D: A rake detained at a station for want of movement instructions

e: A block rake is a full train-load consignment of one party booked from one station to a single destination, so that the rake moves as one unit.

q: The Net Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway are 1,12,00,000 and the tonnes carried are 2,00,000. The average lead of goods traffic is:

options.C: 60 kilometres
options.D: 46 kilometres

e: Average lead of goods traffic = Net Tonne Kilometres / tonnes carried = 1,12,00,000 / 2,00,000 = 56 kilometres.

q: 'Sampark Kranti' Express trains were introduced on Indian Railways primarily to provide:

options.A: Fast services between the State capitals and their district headquarters
options.B: Tourist services connecting the places of religious importance
options.C: Speedy direct connectivity between the States and the national capital, New Delhi
options.D: Suburban services in the metropolitan cities

e: Sampark Kranti Express trains were introduced to give the States speedy direct connectivity with the national capital, New Delhi, with limited intermediate halts.

q: During a period, the locomotives of a railway ran 5,60,000 engine kilometres in use and the engine days in use numbered 1,400. The engine kilometres per engine day in use are:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day in use = 5,60,000 / 1,400 engine days in use = 400.

q: Shatabdi Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fast intercity day trains which return to their originating station on the same day
options.B: Overnight trains connecting the metropolitan cities
options.C: Trains run exclusively for the carriage of parcels and mail
options.D: Fully unreserved trains run on suburban sections

e: Shatabdi Express trains are fast intercity day trains that leave in the morning and return to the originating station the same day.

q: In goods statistics, the 'tonnes carried' over a railway during a period comprise:

options.A: Only the tonnes booked at the stations of that railway
options.B: The tonnes originated on the railway plus the tonnes received from other railways for onward carriage
options.C: Only the tonnes unloaded at the stations of that railway
options.D: The tonnes carried in departmental (non-revenue) trains only

e: Tonnes carried comprise the tonnes originated on the railway plus the tonnes received from other railways for onward carriage during the period.

q: The total cost of the goods services of a railway for a period is Rs 47,50,000 and the Net Tonne Kilometres performed are 19,00,000. The cost per Net Tonne Kilometre is:
e: Cost per Net Tonne Kilometre = total cost of goods services / Net Tonne Kilometres = Rs 47,50,000 / 19,00,000 = Rs 2.50.

q: 'Rajya Rani' Express trains of Indian Railways connect:

options.A: The national capital with the State capitals
options.B: The metropolitan cities with the industrial towns of the country
options.C: The tourist places of a State with the airports
options.D: The State capital with other important cities and towns within the State

e: Rajya Rani Express trains connect the State capital with other important cities and towns within the same State.

q: The goods earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 96,00,000 and the wagon days during the period are 2,40,000. The earnings per wagon day are:

options.C: Rs 45
options.D: Rs 30

e: Earnings per wagon day = goods earnings / wagon days = Rs 96,00,000 / 2,40,000 = Rs 40.

q: MEMU trains on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Diesel multiple unit trains run on unelectrified branch lines
options.B: Electric multiple unit trains run for short and medium distance services on main lines
options.C: Trains hauled by battery-operated locomotives in yards
options.D: Inspection trains run for track-recording purposes

e: MEMU trains are electric multiple unit trains used for short and medium distance services on main line sections, unlike suburban EMU stock.

q: A railway performed 88,00,000 passenger kilometres during a year in which the route kilometres open for traffic were 4,000. The density of passenger traffic on the railway is:

options.C: 2,200 passenger kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: 2,800 passenger kilometres per route kilometre

e: Density of passenger traffic = passenger kilometres / route kilometres = 88,00,000 / 4,000 = 2,200 passenger kilometres per route kilometre.

q: Double-stack container trains, in which containers are carried stacked two high on wagons, are operated on Indian Railways on the:

options.C: Metre-gauge sections of the North Eastern Railway
options.D: Western Dedicated Freight Corridor

e: Double-stack container operation, needing high clearances and electrification headroom, is run on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor.

q: In the operating statistics of Indian Railways, the reliability of locomotives in service is commonly assessed by the index of:

options.A: Engine failures per lakh engine kilometres run
options.C: Engines under repair as a percentage of engines on line
options.D: Fuel consumed per thousand gross tonne kilometres

e: Locomotive reliability in service is judged by the incidence of engine failures per lakh engine kilometres run; fewer failures mean better reliability.

q: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed on a railway during a year were 2,40,00,000 and the route kilometres open for traffic were 6,000. The density of goods traffic on the railway is:

options.A: 3,500 gross tonne kilometres per route kilometre
options.B: 4,000 gross tonne kilometres per route kilometre
options.C: 4,500 gross tonne kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: 3,000 gross tonne kilometres per route kilometre

e: Density of goods traffic = Gross Tonne Kilometres / route kilometres = 2,40,00,000 / 6,000 = 4,000 GTKM per route kilometre.

q: In container traffic on Indian Railways, 'EXIM' containers are those which:

options.A: Are owned by the Container Corporation of India
options.B: Are used exclusively for domestic trade
options.C: Carry export and import traffic between the gateway ports and the inland container depots
options.D: Are carried only in departmental trains

e: EXIM containers carry export and import traffic moving between the gateway ports and the inland container depots.

q: A railway performed 49,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the seat kilometres offered were 70,00,000. The load factor (occupation ratio) of the coaching services is:

options.C: 80 per cent
options.D: 70 per cent

e: Load factor = passenger kilometres / seat kilometres offered x 100 = 49,00,000 / 70,00,000 x 100 = 70 per cent.

q: The 'Palace on Wheels' of Indian Railways is:

options.A: A luxury tourist train operated on the tourist circuits of Rajasthan
options.B: A special train run for the use of foreign tourists between Delhi and Agra only
options.C: An inspection saloon attached to trains for the use of the Railway Minister
options.D: A train carrying exhibitions on science and technology to different places

e: The Palace on Wheels is a luxury tourist train operated on the tourist circuits of Rajasthan.

q: On Indian Railways, the Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of diesel locomotives is compiled separately for:

options.B: Trains run during the day and during the night
options.C: Passenger (coaching) services and goods services
options.D: Trains hauled by different classes of locomotives only

e: Specific Fuel Consumption of diesel locomotives is compiled separately for passenger (coaching) and goods services, as consumption behaviour differs between the two.

q: During a period, the total wagon kilometres run on a railway were 90,00,000, of which the empty wagon kilometres were 36,00,000. The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres is:

options.C: 45 per cent
options.D: 30 per cent

e: Percentage of empty wagon kilometres = 36,00,000 / 90,00,000 x 100 = 40 per cent.
